reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first four premises via CALPHAD predictions and experimental observations of α-Ti precipitation, interstitial diffusion, and PFZ formation. The final premise linking PFZs to brittle fracture is not directly evidenced in E1, which only describes microstructural evolution, not mechanical behavior.
premises: Oxygen and nitrogen stabilize α-Ti phase in Ti-V-Nb-Ta at aging temperature
Interstitials diffuse with Ti to grain boundaries during aging
Grain boundary α-Ti precipitates form and drain adjacent matrix of interstitials
Depletion creates precipitate-free zones (PFZs) lacking solid-solution strengthening
PFZs cause local mechanical weakness promoting brittle intergranular fracture
